value.tellUser:
Peer session `worker-1` is running in `lab-repo/`. It's in its own herdr workspace (wF1, pane wF1:p1), so your current screen didn't change. It was ready in 0s and hasn't been sent a brief yet.

The session stays up until you tell me to stop it. While it's idle it uses no tokens, but it does take up a workspace. Once you send it a brief, it does that work in its own context.

This harness may not let SendMessage reach it by name. If that happens, drive it with `herdr agent prompt worker-1 <text>`, then `herdr agent wait worker-1` and `herdr agent read worker-1`.

To shut it down, run:
  herdr workspace close wF1
  python3 ~/.claude/skills/peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py
The teardown the script printed has no `kill` line, and closing the workspace may leave the claude process running. Check with peer-addr.py and kill any leftover worker-1 PID.

To resume it after a reboot: cd lab-repo && claude --resume worker-1
